title: Authenticated payroll read endpoints expose payroll-run and per-employee pay data without server permission checks
scope: Bounded static check of payroll GET routes, query service, caller session binding, UI read/action gating, and create-existing-run early return; distinct from settlement-versus-payroll overlap.

assessment.mechanics: GET /api/payroll-runs, /{runId}, and /{runId}/lines call PayrollQueryService methods without actor identity or permission checks. PayrollQueryService returns payroll metadata and per-employee base, overtime, extras, deductions, net payable, status, and paid timestamp. AuthenticationMiddleware still requires a valid session, but only binds a declared actor ID when one is present; the GET routes declare none. Thus a caller with any valid session can invoke these endpoints directly.
assessment.additional: CreatePayrollHandler checks for an existing non-cancelled run and returns its DTO before loading or authorizing the actor, so even the POST replay/no-op path can disclose existing run metadata to a session holder lacking employees_manage. The UI gates create/approve/pay actions but calls GET runs and lines on load/selection without those checks.
assessment.policy: Source shows permission gates for create, transition, approval, and pay, and the payroll UI treats those as distinct action permissions. No explicit payroll-read permission or documented policy allowing all authenticated users to inspect individual compensation was located. Treat intended read authorization as requiring owner confirmation, but server absence of a gate is source-confirmed.
assessment.impact: Potential confidentiality exposure of employee pay figures, deductions, approval/payment state, and run metadata to any authenticated cashier/user with a valid session. No financial state mutation is involved in the GET paths.
assessment.counterevidence: Session middleware prevents anonymous API access and rejects a mismatched actorUserId when the route declares one. UI action buttons are permission-gated. Neither countermeasure prevents direct GET invocation because these endpoints supply no actor field and no server permission guard.
assessment.tests: PayrollVerticalSliceTests verifies employees_manage for creating a new run, payroll_approve for approval, and payroll_pay for payout. It does not test read endpoint authorization; the existing-run early-return path is also not covered by the create permission test.
assessment.recommendation: Define a payroll-read permission (or explicitly authorize an existing management permission) and enforce it in all payroll list/detail/line endpoints and before returning a pre-existing run from create. Add tests proving a session-only cashier cannot read run metadata or salary lines, while permitted payroll roles can.

evidence.observation: POST create handles request but GET payroll list, run, and lines directly call query service with no actorUserId or permission gate.
Read service has no actor argument and projects all runs and detailed payroll line amounts.
Existing-period run lookup and return precedes actor lookup and employees_manage authorization.
All /api requests require valid issued session; actor matching only applies to named query/body fields. GET payroll routes have no actor field to match.
Client permission predicates gate manage/approve/pay actions; LoadAsync and selected-run loading call run/line GET APIs without those predicates.
Existing tests cover create/approve/pay action authorization only; no GET read permission coverage, and create test uses a period without an existing run.
